mainTopic: שמיני ספק שביעי in חוץ לארץ (sitting in the סוכה without a ברכה), and why שמיני עצרת is a separate holiday that gets זמן.
overview: Outside ארץ ישראל, the eighth day (שמיני עצרת) might really be the seventh day of סוכות. This is called שמיני ספק שביעי. The גמרא gives two versions of the מחלוקת about this day. In one version, everyone agrees we sit in the סוכה and the argument is about the ברכה. In the other version, everyone agrees there is no ברכה and the argument is about sitting. The final הלכה is that we sit in the סוכה but do not make the ברכה. Next, רבי יוחנן rules that we say שהחיינו (זמן) on שמיני עצרת but not on the seventh day of פסח, because שמיני עצרת is a holiday of its own. The גמרא proves this in several ways: the eighth day's מצוות are different, it breaks from the day right before it, and the פסוקים about its offerings use different wording. The amud ends with a ברייתא in which רבי יהודה calls שמיני a רגל בפני עצמו, with its own קרבן, שיר, ברכה, and לינה.

steps.title: The first version: the argument is about the blessing
steps.stepSummary: Everyone agrees we sit in the סוכה on שמיני ספק שביעי. The argument is whether we also make the ברכה. The one who treats the day as שביעי for סוכה says we bless. The one who treats it as שמיני for both says we do not bless.
steps.simpleTranslation: [They argue] about making the blessing. The one who says it is 'seventh' for the סוכה says we also make the blessing. The one who says it is 'eighth' for both this and that says we do not make the blessing.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא finishes explaining where the two opinions disagree. Since both sides agree we sit in the סוכה, the only open question is the ברכה.
steps.deeperAnalysis: If the day counts as סוכות regarding סוכה, it gets the full מצוה, including the ברכה. If the day counts as שמיני עצרת for everything, we only sit because of the doubt, and a ברכה would be out of place. The disagreement is about how strongly we treat the doubt.

keyTerms.meaning: the eighth day, which outside ארץ ישראל might really be the seventh
for this and for that (for both sitting and blessing)

steps.confusionAlert: This amud starts in the middle of a sentence. The previous line said that everyone agrees we SIT in the סוכה. The only question here is the ברכה.

phrases.english: [they argue] about making the blessing.
phrases.notes: Finishes the sentence: 'Everyone agrees we sit; where they argue is about blessing.'

phrases.english: According to the one who says it is 'seventh' regarding the sukkah —
we also make the blessing,
according to the one who says it is 'eighth' for this and for that —
we do not make the blessing.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Completes the explanation, begun on the previous amud, of where the two opinions disagree.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: Version 1: both sides agree we sit. The view of שביעי לסוכה requires a ברכה. The view of שמיני לזה ולזה says no ברכה.

steps.title: רב יוסף: follow רבי יוחנן, as the great rabbis sat without blessing
steps.stepSummary: רב יוסף rules like רבי יוחנן (no ברכה). His proof is that רב הונא בר ביזנא and the great rabbis of the generation sat in a סוכה on שמיני ספק שביעי and did not make the ברכה.
steps.simpleTranslation: רב יוסף said: Hold on to רבי יוחנן's view. For רב הונא בר ביזנא and all the great rabbis of the generation happened to be in a סוכה on the eighth day, which might be the seventh. They sat, but they did not make the blessing.
steps.whatsHappening: רב יוסף decides the הלכה like רבי יוחנן, who holds שמיני לזה ולזה, so no ברכה. He proves it from what the great rabbis actually did.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The rabbis' behavior matches the first version's dispute exactly. They sat, which both sides agree to. They did not bless, which matches רבי יוחנן. Their conduct is used as a real-life proof (מעשה רב).

keyTerms.meaning: take it in your hand, meaning adopt this view as practice
the great sages of the generation

phrases.english: Rav Yosef said:
Take [the view] of Rabbi Yoḥanan in your hand,
phrases.notes: רבי יוחנן holds שמיני לזה ולזה, so no blessing.

phrases.english: for Rav Huna bar Bizna
and all the great ones of the generation
happened to be in a sukkah
on the eighth day that might be the seventh.
They were sitting [there],
but they did not make the blessing.

steps.triggerLanguage: אָמַר רַב יוֹסֵף: נְקוֹט דְּרַבִּי יוֹחָנָן בְּיָדְךָ
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Decides the dispute from step 1 and brings a practical proof.
steps.raayaObject: That the הלכה follows רבי יוחנן: no ברכה on שמיני ספק שביעי.
steps.raayaSupportSource: The behavior of רב הונא בר ביזנא and the great rabbis of the generation, who sat without blessing.

steps.title: Maybe they skipped the blessing for a different reason
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא questions the proof. Perhaps the rabbis held the view that once a person blesses on the first day of יום טוב, he does not bless again on later days. Then their silence says nothing about שמיני.
steps.simpleTranslation: But perhaps they held like the one who says: once a person has made the blessing on the first day of יום טוב, he no longer makes it again?
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא attacks רב יוסף's proof. It suggests another explanation for why the rabbis did not make a ברכה.
steps.deeperAnalysis: There is a known view that the ברכה on the סוכה is said only once, on the first night of the חג. If the rabbis held that view, they would skip the ברכה on any later day, not specifically because it was שמיני. Then the story cannot prove רבי יוחנן is right.

keyTerms.meaning: he does not make the blessing again

phrases.english: But perhaps they hold
like the one who says:
once he made the blessing on the first day of the Festival
he does not make the blessing again?

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Challenges the proof brought in step 2.
steps.kashyaTarget: רב יוסף's proof from the rabbis' behavior.
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: Their failure to bless may come from the view that the ברכה is said only on the first day. If so, it has nothing to do with the status of שמיני.

steps.title: They had just come from the fields
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא answers that by tradition these rabbis had come in from the fields. This was their first time sitting in a סוכה this חג. Even by the 'bless only once' view they should have blessed, so the proof stands.
steps.simpleTranslation: We have a tradition that they had come from the fields.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא defends רב יוסף's proof. These rabbis had not yet sat in a סוכה during the חג at all.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Even the view that you bless only once agrees that a person blesses the first time he sits. Since this was their first time, their not blessing can only be because they treated the day as שמיני. So the proof for רבי יוחנן holds.

keyTerms.meaning: they came from the field or meadow (where they were herding)

phrases.english: We have a tradition that they came from the fields.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers the challenge of step 3 and restores the proof of step 2.
steps.terutzResolutionType: Factual clarification of the story's circumstances.
steps.terutzHavaAmina: Their silence might just reflect the 'bless only on the first day' view.
steps.terutzMaskana: This was their first time in a סוכה this חג, so they skipped the ברכה only because of שמיני's status.

steps.title: The second version: the argument is about sitting
steps.stepSummary: The second version says everyone agrees there is no ברכה. The argument is whether we sit in the סוכה at all. The view of שביעי לסוכה says we sit. The view of שמיני לזה ולזה says we do not even sit.
steps.simpleTranslation: Some say: Regarding blessing, everyone agrees that we do not bless. Where they argue is about sitting. According to the one who says 'seventh' for the סוכה, we sit. According to the one who says 'eighth' for both, we do not even sit.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא opens a second version (איכא דאמרי) of the whole מחלוקת. It moves the argument to a different place.
steps.deeperAnalysis: In version 1 the floor was 'we sit,' and the debate was about the ברכה. In version 2 the floor is 'no ברכה,' and the debate is about whether we sit. Here the view of שמיני לזה ולזה is stricter about treating the day as שמיני, so we would not sit at all.
steps.confusionAlert: Do not mix up the two versions. Version 1: everyone sits, and the argument is about the ברכה. Version 2: no one blesses, and the argument is about sitting.

phrases.english: Some say:
regarding blessing, everyone agrees
that we do not make the blessing.
Where they argue is about sitting.
According to the one who says 'seventh' regarding the sukkah —
we sit,
and according to the one who says 'eighth' for this and for that —
we do not even sit.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Gives a competing version of the dispute presented in step 1.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: Version 2: no one blesses. The view of שביעי לסוכה requires sitting. The view of שמיני לזה ולזה says not even to sit.

steps.title: רב יוסף: the master of the teaching sat outside the סוכה
steps.stepSummary: In this version too, רב יוסף says to follow רבי יוחנן, whose view here means not sitting. His proof is that רב יהודה בריה דרב שמואל בר שילת sat outside the סוכה on שמיני ספק שביעי. He is the master of the opposing teaching.
steps.simpleTranslation: רב יוסף said: Hold on to רבי יוחנן's view. For who is the master of this teaching? רב יהודה, son of רב שמואל בר שילת. And on the eighth day that might be the seventh, he sat outside the סוכה.
steps.whatsHappening: Within the second version, רב יוסף again rules like רבי יוחנן. He proves it from the conduct of the rabbi who taught the opposing view: even he sat outside the סוכה.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Since רבי יוחנן holds שמיני לזה ולזה, in this version his view means we do not sit in the סוכה. רב יהודה בריה דרב שמואל בר שילת is the one who reported the opposing view (שביעי לסוכה) in רב's name. Yet he himself sat outside the סוכה on this day. If even the master of the opposing teaching acted like רבי יוחנן, that is strong proof for רבי יוחנן.

phrases.english: Rav Yosef said:
Take [the view] of Rabbi Yoḥanan in your hand,
for who is the master of this teaching?

phrases.aramaic: רַב יְהוּדָה בְּרֵיהּ דְּרַב שְׁמוּאֵל בַּר שִׁילַת,
phrases.english: Rav Yehuda, son of Rav Shmuel bar Sheilat,
and on the eighth day that might be the seventh
he sits outside the sukkah.

steps.triggerLanguage: אָמַר רַב יוֹסֵף: נְקוֹט דְּרַבִּי יוֹחָנָן בִּידָךְ
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Decides the version 2 dispute, matching the way רב יוסף ruled in step 2.
steps.raayaObject: That the הלכה in version 2 follows רבי יוחנן: we do not sit in the סוכה.
steps.raayaSupportSource: The conduct of רב יהודה בריה דרב שמואל בר שילת, master of the opposing teaching (שביעי לסוכה), who himself sat outside the סוכה.

steps.title: Final ruling: sit in the סוכה but do not bless
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא rules that on שמיני ספק שביעי we sit in the סוכה but do not make the ברכה.
steps.simpleTranslation: And the הלכה is: we sit [in the סוכה], but we do not make the blessing.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא gives the final practical הלכה after both versions.
steps.deeperAnalysis: This ruling matches the first version, decided like רבי יוחנן, and rejects the second version's idea of not sitting at all. We sit because of the doubt that it may be the seventh day. We do not bless because the day is really treated as שמיני עצרת.
steps.whatToRemember: On שמיני עצרת in חוץ לארץ (שמיני ספק שביעי), we sit in the סוכה but do NOT say the ברכה of לישב בסוכה.
steps.whyThisMatters: This is the source for the common practice in חוץ לארץ of eating in the סוכה on שמיני עצרת without a ברכה.

phrases.english: And the halakha is: we sit,
but we do not make the blessing.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Settles the practical law after both versions of the dispute.
steps.maskanaFinalTakeaway: On שמיני ספק שביעי we sit in the סוכה without a ברכה.

steps.title: רבי יוחנן: say שהחיינו on שמיני עצרת, not on the seventh of פסח
steps.stepSummary: רבי יוחנן rules that we say זמן (שהחיינו) on שמיני עצרת because it is its own holiday. We do not say it on the seventh day of פסח, which is just a continuation of פסח.
steps.simpleTranslation: רבי יוחנן said: We say זמן on the eighth day of the חג, but we do not say זמן on the seventh day of פסח.
steps.whatsHappening: A new statement begins on a related topic: the ברכה of שהחיינו on the last festival days.
steps.deeperAnalysis: שהחיינו is said for a new holiday. שמיני עצרת counts as a separate holiday from סוכות, so it gets its own שהחיינו. The seventh day of פסח is still part of פסח, so it does not.

keyTerms.meaning: the blessing שהחיינו (for reaching this time)
the eighth day of the festival (שמיני עצרת)

steps.whyThisMatters: This rule shows that שמיני עצרת is its own holiday. That idea also stands behind the earlier view of 'שמיני לזה ולזה'.

phrases.english: Rabbi Yoḥanan said:
we say [the blessing of] 'time' on the eighth day of the Festival,
but we do not say [the blessing of] 'time'
on the seventh day of Pesach.

steps.triggerLanguage: אָמַר רַבִּי יוֹחָנָן: אוֹמְרִים זְמַן בִּשְׁמִינִי שֶׁל חַג
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Starts a new related topic about the ברכה of זמן on the final festival days.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: Say שהחיינו on שמיני עצרת, but not on שביעי של פסח.

steps.title: Proof: The eighth day is different in three ways
steps.stepSummary: רבי לוי בר חמא (or רבי חמא בר חנינא) proves that שמיני עצרת is its own holiday. Three מצוות of סוכות do not apply on it: סוכה, לולב, and ניסוך המים.
steps.simpleTranslation: And רבי לוי בר חמא said, and some say it was רבי חמא בר חנינא: Know that the eighth day is its own holiday, because it is different in three things: סוכה, לולב, and the water pouring.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא brings a proof for רבי יוחנן's ruling that שמיני עצרת is its own holiday. The proof is that three special מצוות of סוכות stop on that day.
steps.deeperAnalysis: If the eighth day were just one more day of סוכות, its מצוות would continue. Instead, there is no סוכה obligation, no לולב, and no ניסוך המים. A day with its own set of rules counts as a separate holiday, so it gets its own זמן.

keyTerms.meaning: Know (a word that introduces a supporting proof)
The water pouring on the מזבח during סוכות

steps.whyThisMatters: This sets up the whole section's test for a separate holiday: a day is separate if its מצוות are different.

phrases.english: And Rabbi Levi bar Chama said
and some say it was Rabbi Chama bar Chanina:
Know this, for it is different in three things:
phrases.notes: "It" means שמיני עצרת, compared to the seven days of סוכות.

phrases.english: in סוכה, and לולב, and the water pouring.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Supports רבי יוחנן's ruling in Step 8 that שמיני עצרת is its own holiday
steps.raayaObject: רבי יוחנן's claim that שמיני עצרת is a separate holiday and so gets זמן
steps.raayaSupportSource: Three מצוות of סוכות do not apply on the eighth day: סוכה, לולב, ניסוך המים

steps.title: Even by רבי יהודה's view, two differences remain
steps.stepSummary: רבי יהודה holds that the water was poured on all eight days. Even so, the eighth day still differs in two things, סוכה and לולב, so the proof still works.
steps.simpleTranslation: And according to רבי יהודה, who said the כהן poured a לוג of water on all eight days, the eighth day is still different in two things.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא blocks a problem before anyone raises it. By רבי יהודה's view, the water pouring continues on the eighth day, so that difference falls away. The other two differences are still there.
steps.deeperAnalysis: רבי יהודה removes one of the three differences, since by him ניסוך המים happens on the eighth day too. סוכה and לולב still stop, so the eighth day still has its own rules. The proof survives with two differences instead of three.

keyTerms.meaning: A measure of liquid (about the volume of six eggs)
Pours (as a libation on the מזבח)

phrases.english: And according to Rabbi Yehuda, who said:
"With a log he would pour all eight days,"
it is still different in two things.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Adjusts the proof from Step 9 so it also works by רבי יהודה's view
steps.terutzResolutionType: Narrowing the proof: fewer differences, but enough to stand
steps.terutzHavaAmina: Since רבי יהודה has water pouring on all eight days, the proof might seem to fall apart by his view
steps.terutzMaskana: Two differences, סוכה and לולב, are enough to make the eighth day separate

steps.title: Challenge: The seventh day of Pesach is also different
steps.stepSummary: If differences make a day separate, the seventh day of פסח should be separate too. Eating מצה is required only on the first night.
steps.simpleTranslation: If so, the seventh day of פסח should also count as different, because it differs in eating מצה. As the Master said: on the first night it is required, and from then on it is optional.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא attacks the proof's logic. By the same test, the seventh day of פסח should also be its own holiday and get זמן, yet רבי יוחנן said it does not.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The test was "a different מצוה means a separate holiday." On פסח, eating מצה is required only on the first night. After that it is optional, so the seventh day also differs from the start of the holiday. The test seems to prove too much.

keyTerms.meaning: If so (if your reasoning is right)

steps.confusionAlert: "Optional" applies only to eating מצה. Eating חמץ is still forbidden all seven days.

phrases.aramaic: אִי הָכִי, שְׁבִיעִי שֶׁל פֶּסַח נָמֵי:
phrases.english: If so, the seventh day of Pesach too:
it is different in eating matza!
For the Master said: the first night is an obligation,
from then on it is optional.

steps.triggerLanguage: אִי הָכִי, שְׁבִיעִי שֶׁל פֶּסַח נָמֵי
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Challenges the test used in Steps 9-10
steps.kashyaTarget: The proof that differing מצוות make a day a separate holiday
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: The seventh day of פסח also differs, since מצה is no longer required, yet it gets no זמן. So the test must be flawed.

steps.title: Answer: Pesach differs only from the first night
steps.stepSummary: The cases are not alike. The seventh day of פסח differs only from the first night, not from the first day. שמיני עצרת differs even from the daytime of סוכות.
steps.simpleTranslation: How can you compare them? There, the seventh day differs from the first night, but not from the first day. Here, the eighth day differs even from the daytime.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא answers the challenge by showing the two cases are not the same. The difference on פסח is much smaller.
steps.deeperAnalysis: On פסח, the required מצה is only on the first night. The first day itself is already optional, just like the seventh day, so the seventh day matches the first day exactly. On סוכות, סוכה and לולב apply in the daytime too, so the eighth day differs from the first day as well.

keyTerms.meaning: How can you compare? (rejecting a comparison)

phrases.english: How can you compare?!
There, it differs from the night,
from the day it does not differ.
Here, it differs even from the day too.

steps.terutzHavaAmina: Any difference at all would make a day separate, so the seventh day of פסח should count
steps.terutzMaskana: A day is separate only if it differs even from the daytime of the holiday, and only שמיני עצרת does

steps.title: רבינא: שמיני עצרת differs from the day right before it
steps.stepSummary: רבינא gives another answer. שמיני עצרת differs from the seventh day, the day right before it. The seventh day of פסח differs only from the first day, not from the sixth day before it.
steps.simpleTranslation: רבינא said: This one, שמיני עצרת, differs from the day before it. That one, the seventh day of פסח, differs only from a day earlier than the one before it.
steps.whatsHappening: רבינא offers a different way to answer the challenge about פסח. He compares each day to the day just before it.
steps.deeperAnalysis: On the seventh day of סוכות you sit in the סוכה and take the לולב, and the next day you do not. So שמיני עצרת is a sharp change from the day before. The sixth and seventh days of פסח are exactly the same; only the first day was different. A day that matches the day before it is just a continuation.

keyTerms.meaning: From the day before the day before it (an earlier day)

phrases.english: Ravina said: This one differs from the day before it,
and that one differs only from an earlier day.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: A second answer to the challenge in Step 11, parallel to Step 12
steps.terutzResolutionType: Distinguishing the cases by comparing each day to the one right before it
steps.terutzMaskana: שמיני עצרת breaks sharply from the seventh day of סוכות. The seventh day of פסח is the same as the sixth.

steps.title: רב פפא: One bull versus many bulls
steps.stepSummary: רב פפא brings a proof from the תורה's offerings. On שמיני עצרת the תורה says one bull ("פר"). On סוכות it says bulls ("פרים").
steps.simpleTranslation: רב פפא said: Here, on שמיני עצרת, it is written "a bull." There, on סוכות, it is written "bulls."
steps.whatsHappening: רב פפא gives a third reason, taken from the תורה, that שמיני עצרת is its own holiday. This also answers why פסח is different.
steps.deeperAnalysis: On סוכות the number of bulls goes down by one each day, from 13 down to 7. If the eighth day were part of סוכות, it should have 6 bulls. Instead it has just one, so the תורה itself treats it as a new holiday. פסח has the same offerings every day, so its seventh day is a continuation.
steps.whatToRemember: שמיני עצרת is its own holiday and gets זמן. The proofs are: (1) the מצוות of סוכות stop on it, even in the daytime; (2) it breaks from the day right before it (רבינא); (3) its offering is one bull, not a continuation of the bulls of סוכות (רב פפא). The seventh day of פסח is just a continuation of פסח.
steps.whyThisMatters: This is why we say שהחיינו on the night of שמיני עצרת but not on the seventh day of פסח.

phrases.english: (Rav Pappa said:) Here it is written "a bull,"
phrases.notes: במדבר כ״ט:ל״ו, the offering of שמיני עצרת

phrases.english: there it is written "bulls."
phrases.notes: במדבר כ״ט:י״ג and onward: 13 bulls going down to 7 over the days of סוכות

steps.relationToPreviousStep: A third answer showing שמיני עצרת is separate, alongside Steps 12 and 13
steps.terutzResolutionType: Proof from a verse that sets the day apart
steps.terutzMaskana: The תורה gives שמיני עצרת its own offering, one bull, which marks it as its own holiday

steps.title: The missing ו in the verse about the eighth day
steps.stepSummary: רב נחמן בר יצחק brings another proof that שמיני עצרת is separate. For the eighth day the verse says ״בַּיּוֹם״, but for the other days it says ״וּבַיּוֹם״.
steps.simpleTranslation: רב נחמן בר יצחק said: Here, about the eighth day, it is written ״בַּיּוֹם״ ("on the day"). There, about the other days, it is written ״וּבַיּוֹם״ ("and on the day").
steps.whatsHappening: Another אמורא adds one more proof from the פסוקים that שמיני עצרת stands alone.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The letter ו means "and." It links each day of סוכות to the day before it, so days two through seven form one chain. The eighth day starts without ו, so it is not linked to that chain. It begins a new unit.

keyTerms.meaning: Here (this verse, about the eighth day)
There (the other verses, about the days of סוכות)
And on the day. The ו links it to what came before

phrases.english: Rav Naḥman bar Yitzḥak said:
Here it is written: "On the day,"
there it is written: "And on the day."
phrases.notes: The other days of סוכות are joined with ו

steps.triggerLanguage: רַב נַחְמָן בַּר יִצְחָק אָמַר, הָכָא כְּתִיב
steps.relationToPreviousStep: A parallel proof from the verses, in the same style as רב פפא's proof from פר versus פרים
steps.terutzHavaAmina: One could think the eighth day is just the last day of סוכות
steps.terutzMaskana: The missing ו shows the eighth day is not joined to the earlier days

steps.title: "As the regulation" versus "as their regulation"
steps.stepSummary: רב אשי brings another proof. For the eighth day the verse says ״כַּמִּשְׁפָּט״, but for the seventh day it says ״כְּמִשְׁפָּטָם״.
steps.simpleTranslation: רב אשי said: Here, about the eighth day, it is written ״כַּמִּשְׁפָּט״ ("as the regulation"). There, about the seventh day, it is written ״כְּמִשְׁפָּטָם״ ("as their regulation").
steps.whatsHappening: One more אמורא gives one more proof from a small change in wording.
steps.deeperAnalysis: ״כְּמִשְׁפָּטָם״ ends in "their." That ending ties the seventh day's offerings to the offerings of all the earlier days, as one group. On the eighth day that ending is missing. So its offerings have a rule of their own.

keyTerms.meaning: As the regulation (said about the eighth day)
As their regulation (said about the seventh day; groups the days together)

phrases.english: Rav Ashi said:
Here it is written: "as the regulation,"
there it is written: "as their regulation."

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Another parallel textual proof, added after רב נחמן בר יצחק's proof
steps.terutzHavaAmina: The eighth day's offerings might be part of the סוכות group
steps.terutzMaskana: Without "their," the eighth day's offerings stand alone
steps.whatToRemember: Four אמוראים, four proofs that שמיני עצרת is separate. The day before it is different (רבינא). פר versus פרים (רב פפא). ביום versus וביום (רב נחמן בר יצחק). כמשפט versus כמשפטם (רב אשי).

steps.title: A ברייתא about the bulls that might support this view
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא suggests a ברייתא as support. The תנא קמא says the bulls, rams, and lambs all hold each other back. רבי יהודה says the bulls do not, because their number goes down each day.
steps.simpleTranslation: Shall we say a ברייתא supports him? The ברייתא says: The bulls, the rams, and the lambs hold each other back. רבי יהודה says: The bulls do not hold each other back, because their number keeps going down.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא brings a ברייתא that may support the view that שמיני עצרת is a separate festival. This step only sets up the ברייתא. The supporting line comes at its end.
steps.deeperAnalysis: "Hold each other back" means that if one type of animal is missing, the others do not count either. The תנא קמא says all three types depend on each other. רבי יהודה says the bulls are different. Their number drops every day (13, 12, 11, down to 7), which shows the תורה is flexible about them.

keyTerms.meaning: Shall we say this supports him?
They hold each other back. Without one, the others do not count
They keep going down in number

steps.confusionAlert: Do not look for the support in רבי יהודה's first statement about the bulls. The support comes from his answer at the end of the ברייתא, where he says שמיני is a festival of its own.

phrases.english: Shall we say this supports him:
phrases.notes: Supports the view that שמיני עצרת is a separate festival

phrases.english: the bulls, the rams, and the lambs
hold each other back.
And Rabbi Yehuda says:

phrases.aramaic: פָּרִים אֵין מְעַכְּבִין זֶה אֶת זֶה,
phrases.english: the bulls do not hold the others back,
since they keep going down in number.
phrases.notes: 13 bulls on the first day, one fewer each day, down to 7

steps.relationToPreviousStep: After the proofs from the verses, the גמרא looks for support from a תנאי source
steps.raayaObject: The view that שמיני עצרת is a festival of its own
steps.raayaSupportSource: A ברייתא with a מחלוקת between the תנא קמא and רבי יהודה about whether the offerings hold each other back

steps.title: The חכמים say all the animals go down on the eighth day
steps.stepSummary: The חכמים challenge רבי יהודה. On the eighth day the rams and lambs also go down in number, so by his logic they should not hold back either.
steps.simpleTranslation: They said to him: But don't all of them go down in number on the eighth day!
steps.whatsHappening: Inside the ברייתא, the חכמים push back on רבי יהודה's reason.
steps.deeperAnalysis: רבי יהודה said the bulls are different because their number drops. But on the eighth day the rams drop from 2 to 1 and the lambs drop from 14 to 7. If dropping in number means "does not hold back," then the rams and lambs should not hold back either.

keyTerms.meaning: But isn't it so that... (opens a challenge)

phrases.english: They said to him: But don't all of them
go down in number on the eighth day!

steps.triggerLanguage: אָמְרוּ לוֹ: וַהֲלֹא כּוּלָּן מִתְמַעֲטִין וְהוֹלְכִין בַּשְּׁמִינִי
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Attacks the reason רבי יהודה gave in the ברייתא
steps.kashyaTarget: רבי יהודה's reason that the bulls do not hold back because they decrease
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: On the eighth day every type decreases, so his rule should cover all the animals, not just the bulls

steps.title: רבי יהודה: the eighth day is a festival of its own
steps.stepSummary: רבי יהודה answers that שמיני is a separate festival, so its smaller numbers are not a decrease. Like the seven days, it has its own קרבן, שיר, ברכה, and לינה.
steps.simpleTranslation: He said to them: The eighth day is a festival of its own. Just as the seven days of the festival need an offering, a song, a blessing, and staying overnight, so too the eighth day needs an offering, a song, a blessing, and staying overnight.
steps.whatsHappening: רבי יהודה answers the חכמים. His answer is the line the גמרא wanted as support that שמיני עצרת is separate.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The rams and lambs on the eighth day are not a smaller version of the סוכות offerings. They belong to a new festival with its own set of offerings. Only the bulls truly decrease within the seven days. רבי יהודה backs this up with four things the eighth day has on its own. The ברכה there may be the שהחיינו blessing, which is why this looks like support.
steps.whyThisMatters: "Festival of its own" is the idea the whole sugya has been building toward. If the ברכה here means שהחיינו, this ברייתא supports saying שהחיינו on שמיני עצרת.
steps.whatToRemember: רבי יהודה says שמיני is a רגל בפני עצמו, with its own קרבן, שיר, ברכה, and לינה. This is the source the גמרא hopes will support the view that the eighth day is separate.

phrases.aramaic: אָמַר לָהֶן: שְׁמִינִי רֶגֶל בִּפְנֵי עַצְמוֹ הוּא.
phrases.english: He said to them: The eighth day is a festival of its own.
For just as the seven days of the festival
need an offering and a song
and a blessing and staying overnight,
so too the eighth day needs an offering and a song
and a blessing and staying overnight.

steps.triggerLanguage: אָמַר לָהֶן: שְׁמִינִי רֶגֶל בִּפְנֵי עַצְמוֹ הוּא
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers the challenge of the חכמים inside the ברייתא
steps.terutzResolutionType: Reframing: the eighth day is a new unit, not a decrease
steps.terutzHavaAmina: The smaller numbers on the eighth day look like a decrease in all the animals
steps.terutzMaskana: The eighth day is a separate festival with its own offerings, so only the bulls truly decrease
